provenance.rule: a provenance chain is printed with its gaps: an SBOM whose commit nobody recorded cannot be re-built, and saying so is the finding

owners.rule: ownership is an evidenced path from an application to the component; a component nobody reaches is a component nobody has deployed
not_proven: that the repository which produced the artifact is the one that holds the component's own source: the SBOM joins them as data, not as provenance

states.statement: pkg:generic/openssl: SBOM_PRESENT, INSTALLED, LOADED, CONFIGURED, RUNTIME_USED; not STATIC_REFERENCED
states.rule: installed, loaded and used are three different facts; a model that promotes one into the next has replaced a measurement with an assumption

versions.statement: pkg:generic/openssl: DECLARED_VERSION=3.0.13, IMAGE_VERSION=—, RUNTIME_VERSION=3.0.11, VENDOR_VERSION=— — 2 versions, preserved
versions.rule: a declared version, an image version and a runtime version are three observations; the conflict is published, not resolved

tree.statement: Payments API: 2 direct, 2 transitive, 2 listed only; pkg:generic/http-core@1.2.0, pkg:generic/openssl reached through another component
tree.rule: a transitive dependency is reported with its path: the direct parent is what a remediation upgrades, and the transitive child is what it fixes

canonical.statement: 44 record(s) resolve to 26 canonical asset(s); 2 carry more than one record; 23 are identified by a name alone and are not merged with anything
canonical.rule: identity is one of digest, image_digest, repository, namespace; a name is a label, and a label merge attributes one team's vulnerability to another
not_proven: that two records with no shared anchor are different assets: they may be one asset nobody recorded an anchor for, and that is a gap in the collection rather than a fact about the estate

vendor.statement: pkg:generic/openssl → OpenSSL 3.x → OpenSSL Project; deployed in 2 deployment(s) across 1 application(s)
vendor.rule: a vendor is reached through the product that supplied the component, and a product with no vendor is a gap rather than a link to invent
not_proven: that the vendor's published version is the one installed: the vendor portal states a product version and the SBOM states a package version, and they are two rows

radius.statement: upgrade pkg:generic/openssl 3.0.13 → 3.0.14: 1 application(s), 1 business system(s), 2 image(s), 1 process(es), 3 algorithm(s), 1 hardware, 1 certificate(s), 1 endpoint(s)
radius.rule: a package upgrade of a crypto library is a crypto change: the blast radius is the walk, and the regression list is derived from it rather than typed in by the reviewer

lifecycle.statement: 49 supply edge(s): FIRST_SEEN 3, ACTIVE 45, SUPERSEDED 1; 1 superseded or removed edge(s) kept
lifecycle.rule: a dependency has a life: a superseded edge keeps the row that replaced it, because a deletion here is an erasure of history

profile.statement: 19 crypto dependency edge(s) across 4 evidence type(s); 3 proven by a runtime or network observation, 16 capability, static, configured or declared
profile.rule: every crypto dependency carries its evidence type: a capability, a static hit, a configured policy and a wire observation are four different facts and are never summed into one number

twin.statement: 44 SBOM node(s) projected from CANONICAL_ESTATE; no twin was supplied to check against
twin.rule: the SBOM is a projection of the canonical estate and the twin: a second database that agrees on the day it is loaded is a second truth waiting to disagree

handoff.statement: pkg:generic/openssl: 3 capability(ies) handed to the CBOM; 1 corroborated by runtime or network evidence
handoff.rule: the SBOM contributes capability and provenance; only a collector contributes usage, and the type travels with the row

pqc.statement: pkg:generic/openssl: 2 quantum-sensitive capability(ies) and 1 observed use(s); the SBOM answers the first and the CBOM answers the second
pqc.rule: the SBOM hands capability to the CBOM and never decides readiness: a listed RSA is a question a migration asks, an observed RSA-2048 is the candidate
not_proven: that a capability is reachable: the component lists it, and no collector has shown a caller using it

limits: the inventory is a fixture: its shapes are the store's, its rows are not
a stored row records what a collector saw when it ran; nothing here re-runs a collector, so a stale row stays a stale row and the class says so
the chain is only as complete as the columns: a row that names no commit stops the provenance there, and the gap is printed rather than filled
the twin is a CBOM projection with its own input shape, so this guide proves the SBOM nodes carry the canonical ids a twin is keyed by, not that a twin was rebuilt from them
